doc:
BVA and 2CDE over the reference file's bursts. Both take the burst bounds as an (n, 2) block; the cases pass them flat and each runner shapes them, the same rule as hist.update and tiff.write_f64.

These could only be tested in Python and JavaScript until the R and Java modules gained BVA.i and TwoCDE.i -- and reaching them from R needed compute_bursts(), because SWIG's R overload dispatcher cannot accept a matrix at all.

cases.doc: One mean proximity ratio per burst. A proximity ratio is a fraction, so the sum over 293 bursts is a strong shape check that no single value can fake.
One 2CDE value per burst, over the same bounds -- so the two features must agree on how many bursts there are, which is the cheapest way to catch a stride error in either.
